title: [YouPass Collect] - Government education spending and youth participation rates
prompt: The table below shows the percentage of government spending on education and training and the participation of 18-24 year olds in five countries in 2002. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the proportion of government expenditure allocated to education and training, as well as the rate of participation among young adults aged 18-24, across five European nations in 2002.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, in terms of expenditure rate, Slovenia dedicated the largest share of its budget to education, while Poland had the lowest government spending in this sector. Regarding participation rate, Poland recorded the highest engagement among young people, whereas Romania and the Czech Republic reported the lowest figures, suggesting no clear correlation between government investment and youth involvement.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding countries with higher youth participation, Poland led with 44% of 18-24 year olds engaged in education or training, followed by Slovenia at 40% and Hungary at 34%, representing a 10 percentage point gap between the highest and lowest in this group. In terms of government expenditure, however, the pattern was completely reversed, with Slovenia allocating a quarter of its budget to this area, nearly double that of Hungary at 13%, and five times that of Poland, which invested merely 5%, the lowest figure among all nations surveyed.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining countries, both the Czech Republic and Romania reported lower participation rates, at 27% and 23% respectively, approximately 11-17 percentage points below the higher-participation group. Their expenditure levels were also relatively modest and nearly equivalent, with Romania spending 10% of its budget on education and training, marginally higher than the Czech Republic's 9%, both falling in the mid-range compared to other nations.
